definition: A scam message — usually email — designed to look like it's from a real company or person, trying to trick you into clicking a link or giving up information.
Phishing sent by text message (SMS) instead of email — the same tricks, like fake delivery notices or bank alerts.
Phishing delivered through a QR code — scanning it sends you to a fake website instead of typing a link yourself.
Faking the caller ID or sender address so a message or call appears to come from someone trustworthy, when it doesn't.
A fake investment where early investors are paid using money from newer investors, not real profit — it collapses once new money stops coming in.
A long-con scam that slowly builds a fake friendship or romance over weeks before steering the victim toward a fake investment.
Using AI to recreate someone's voice from a short audio sample, then using the fake voice to impersonate them on a call.
A direct, fast bank-to-bank money transfer that's very difficult to reverse once sent — a favorite payment method for scammers.
Quick-response code: a square barcode that a phone camera scans to open a link or app.
Artificial intelligence: software that performs tasks that normally need human intelligence.
Uniform resource locator: the web address of a page.
Personal identification number: a short secret code that proves it is you, such as a bank card PIN.
Short message service: ordinary text messages sent between phones.
Long cons in which a scammer builds a fake friendship or romance, then pushes the victim into a fraudulent investment.
